rows.draftLearningTask: Orient a specimen and identify colliculi, peduncles, aqueduct and major internal landmarks.
Compare superior and inferior collicular sections by nuclei, tracts and decussations.
Localize Weber, Benedikt and Parinaud syndromes on sectional maps.
Map brainstem nuclei by level, functional modality and associated nerves.
Identify surfaces, poles, sulci, gyri and functional areas on a model and predict deficits from representative lesions.
Distinguish association, commissural and projection fibres and predict deficits after callosal or internal capsule lesions.
Diagram their major components and connections and relate basal ganglia circuitry to Parkinson disease, chorea, athetosis and ballismus.
Compare subdivisions by boundaries, relations, major nuclei and principal connections.
Identify the arteries forming the circle of Willis on a model and trace major cerebral branches to their territories.
Demonstrate the parts, boundaries and landmarks of the lateral, third and fourth ventricles on sections.
Use ventricular patterns to predict the anatomical level of a congenital CSF obstruction.
Trace olfactory, visual, auditory and gustatory signals to their central targets.
Identify spinal cord, cerebellum and cerebrum slides and justify each identification by its architecture.
Map neural tube regions and vesicles to the cord, brainstem, cerebral hemispheres and cerebellum.
Compare representative open defects by site and mechanism of failed closure.
Classify unknown epithelial slides by layering and cell shape and relate each structure to function.
Identify junctions, surface specializations and basal attachments on electron micrographs and explain their roles.
Distinguish representative connective tissues on slides by cells, fibres and matrix and explain their functions.
Explain how ultrastructural features of fibres, matrix and resident cells support tissue function.
Identify skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle on slides using striation, nuclei and cellular arrangement.
Compare the three muscle types and relate organization to contraction and physiological role.
Compare sarcomeres, membrane systems and contractile anchoring in the three muscle types.
Identify multipolar and pseudounipolar neurons, representative ganglia and peripheral nerve on slides.
Relate dendrites, soma, axon and terminals to signal reception, integration and transmission.
Explain synaptic and myelin organization using representative electron micrographs.
Identify elastic and muscular arteries and capillaries on slides and justify each classification.
Compare arterial, venous and capillary architecture and explain how each supports its haemodynamic role.
Compare endothelial junctions, basal lamina and supporting structures across representative vessel types.
Identify serous, mucous and mixed acini on slides and explain the distinguishing appearances.
Identify lymph node, spleen, thymus and tonsil on slides and explain how their compartments support distinct immune functions.
Identify bone on microscopy, distinguish compact and trabecular organization and relate architecture to load and remodelling.
Identify hyaline, elastic and fibrocartilage on slides and relate their matrices to mechanical roles.
Identify thick and thin skin and their appendages and explain the functional significance of the differences.
Label a metaphase chromosome and classify chromosomes by centromere position.
Sequence specimen preparation, chromosome banding and arrangement and explain what abnormalities a karyotype can detect.
Explain lyonization and use a representative example to relate mosaic expression to phenotype.
Compare Mendelian and non-Mendelian inheritance using representative disorders.
Draw pedigrees for major inheritance modes and annotate representative disorders and transmission clues.
Explain how genetic susceptibility and environmental factors combine in representative multifactorial traits.
Compare genetic mechanisms, inheritance and distinguishing clinical features of achondroplasia, cystic fibrosis and hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets.
Distinguish numerical abnormalities from deletions, duplications, inversions and translocations using diagrams.
Compare the origin of distinct cell lines in mosaicism and chimerism using an example of each.
Match Prader-Willi, Edwards, Patau, Down, Turner and Klinefelter syndromes to their genetic mechanisms and representative clinical features.
Distinguish variant frequency from pathogenicity and compare polymorphism with disease-associated sequence variation.
Compare counselling, karyotyping, FISH, PCR and sequencing by purpose and use a representative case to choose a test.
Order major prenatal and postnatal stages and identify the transitions that separate them.
Distinguish ontogeny from phylogeny and explain trimester and fetal viability in developmental context.
Diagram endometrial changes during menstrual, proliferative and secretory phases.
Align ovarian and endometrial phases on a timeline and explain their hormonal coordination.
Draw spermatogenesis and oogenesis and compare meiotic timing, arrests and products.
Sequence gamete interaction, fusion and zygote formation and explain the consequences for ploidy and developmental activation.
Map representative contraceptive methods to the reproductive structures or events they affect.
Distinguish teratogenic effects from factors affecting fertility, and explain surrogacy and the social interpretation of population sex ratio.
Sequence cleavage, compaction and cavitation and identify the major blastocyst compartments.
Trace trophoblast differentiation and relate the resulting layers to implantation and early exchange.
Diagram normal implantation and distinguish common ectopic sites by anatomy.
Draw the bilaminar disc, extraembryonic mesoderm and coelom and locate the prechordal plate.
Explain the decidual reaction, distinguish early pregnancy loss from normal development and identify the basis of hCG testing.
Diagram streak formation, cell migration and regression and identify the resulting germ layers.
Sequence notochord formation and explain its inductive role and adult remnant.
Draw neural plate folding, tube closure and neural crest separation in developmental order.
Trace segmentation of paraxial mesoderm and the emergence of the embryonic body cavity.
Relate persistent primitive streak, notochord remnants and failed neural closure to teratoma, nucleus pulposus and representative malformations.
Explain how early pregnancy is established, relate teratogenic risk to developmental timing and distinguish the later screening role of maternal serum AFP.
Compare formation, function and fate of chorion, amnion, yolk sac, allantois and decidua.
Trace cord formation and label the vessels, supporting tissue and covering on a cross-section.
Diagram villous development, maternal and fetal circulations and the exchange barrier and explain key placental functions.
Compare dizygotic and monozygotic development and relate timing of embryonic division to chorionicity and amnionicity.
Relate placental hormones to uterine growth, pregnancy maintenance and changes approaching parturition.
Compare age estimation from developmental landmarks and fetal measurements and distinguish gestational from postfertilization age.
Identify central, eccentric, marginal and velamentous insertions on placental diagrams.
Compare screening and diagnostic approaches and distinguish invasive sampling from non-invasive methods.
Explain indications, sample acquisition and limitations of amniocentesis using a labelled anatomical diagram.
Explain indications, access routes, sampled tissue and limitations of chorionic villus sampling.
Demonstrate respectful cadaver and tissue handling under observation, following local procedures for exposure, movement and return of specimens.
